title: Microsoft reportedly projects $1,200 to $1,800 price for 2028 Project Helix
gist: Fortune reports Microsoft internally projects a $1,200 to $1,800 price for its 2028 Project Helix console, following a handheld due by end of next year, amid fights over Windows versus an Xbox-controlled OS and a shift of Game Pass toward a la carte tiers.

insights.claim: Microsoft's Project Helix console, slated for the 2028 holiday season, has an internally projected price of $1,200 to $1,800, which could fall if Microsoft subsidizes it.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: A subsidy-free price at this level would reset the console category from mass-market toward premium PC-like hardware.

insights.claim: The article attributes high prices to the slowing of Moore's Law and AI-driven component shortages: the Steam Machine starts above $1,000, the PS5 Pro is $900 and the six-year-old Xbox Series X is $750.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: AI demand for memory and chips is pushing consumer hardware prices up even on old designs, a cross-sector spillover.

insights.claim: Fortune reports an internal dispute over whether the Helix handheld runs trimmed Windows Home or a bespoke Xbox OS, with one executive threatening to cancel the handheld if forced to use Windows; the Xbox team now largely controls OS direction.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: A custom OS signals Xbox shifting away from Windows dependence, with software-ecosystem implications.

insights.claim: Microsoft has pressed the hardware team to pull Helix timelines forward by at least several months, partly by using AI tools.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Schedule compression through AI tooling is a concrete example of enterprise AI productivity claims.

insights.claim: Game Pass is reported to move toward a heavily tiered a la carte model with add-ons for console-only games, cloud gaming and multiplayer.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Unbundling could raise average revenue from engaged users but erode the all-in-one subscription pitch.

insights.claim: Staff worry that Xbox CEO Asha Sharma was installed to make painful cuts before a sale of an Xbox spinoff, while Judson Althoff denies this.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Divestiture speculation leaves hardware commitments uncertain, so Helix timing carries execution risk.
insights.quote: “We would not have put [Sharma] on a business we intend to sell. There’s going to be a ton of speculation about all this. Time will tell.”
